about.title: Downey Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product should do what the box says it will do. When it doesn't — when a space heater bought at a store off Firestone Boulevard catches fire, when a child's car seat fails on Lakewood Boulevard, when a power tool's guard slips in a garage on Florence Avenue — the harm lands on a Downey family that trusted the label. Product liability claims in California deal with that broken trust. Under strict liability, you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless. Showing the product had a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, and that the defect caused your injury, is usually the core of the case. Responsibility can reach the maker, the distributor, and the retailer that sold it. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Downey residents in Los Angeles County with an independent personal injury attorney who handles product cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Sets a Product Case Apart in Downey

items.title: You usually don't have to prove carelessness
items.desc: California applies strict liability to many product claims, so the question is generally whether the product was defective and caused your injury — not whether the company meant to cut corners.

items.title: The product is the evidence
items.desc: Hold on to the item, its packaging, receipts, and any photos of the scene. A Downey attorney will want to examine the actual product before anyone else does.

items.title: More than one company may answer for it
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer that sold the product can all share responsibility under California law, which matters when one link in that chain has gone out of business or is overseas.

items.question: My car's airbag didn't deploy in a crash on Firestone Boulevard. Is that a product claim or a car accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both. Downey logged 829 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involve a vehicle part that didn't perform as designed. A product liability claim looks at the defect itself, while a separate claim may address the other driver. An attorney can sort out which path fits your situation, but keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until it's inspected.

items.question: What counts as a 'defect' under California law?
items.answer: There are three general types. A design defect means the product is unsafe as planned, a manufacturing defect means something went wrong making that particular unit, and a warning defect means the instructions or labels failed to alert you to a known risk. You typically only need to show one of these applies and that it caused your injury.

items.question: I bought the product used or at a swap meet. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. Strict liability in California is aimed at businesses in the chain of distribution, so the manufacturer may still be responsible even if you weren't the first owner. The details of where and how you got it matter, which is why speaking with an attorney early is helpful. LawProactive can connect you with one for free.
